review_summary: Fixed allowlist contains exactly 70 branches and matches the 70 preflight candidates after excluding explicit hold maint/0.1.
GitHub DELETE endpoint is git/refs/heads/<branch>; it only targets the fixed repository ref and uses no force operation.
Original script rechecked SHA, protected flag, and open PR before DELETE, but did not recheck current-main ancestry, active deletion rulesets, or fresh worktree use at deletion time.
Original script treated every branch API error as possibly not found and did not distinguish already_absent from API failures.
The report blob SHA was not pinned, allowing a rewritten assessment with the same baseline to change the pinned branch SHAs.
No local branch, worktree, tag, manifest, or file deletion/write operation was present in the original script; only the intended GitHub branch-ref DELETE call was mutating.
safety_fixes_in_temporary_copy: Pin the assessment GitHub blob SHA and recheck it immediately before each deletion.
Recheck each candidate SHA against the live main SHA and verify main still descends from the fixed baseline before each deletion.
Read active branch deletion rulesets before the dry-run and again immediately before each deletion; treat ambiguous patterns conservatively.
Refresh the local worktree branch list for each deletion.
Classify HTTP 404 as already_absent and other API failures as errors; stop the remaining batch on API errors or concurrent state conflicts.
Stop after a DELETE API error so later refs are not modified under uncertain state.
